phases.message: That freeze hit the beans and we have corn claims to file. Start here in Fieldmark: read the policy on notices, causes and claims, our units and guarantees, and the notices we've already given.
Now Acrelog. Go through every field: what's harvested and for how many bushels, what's still standing, and the scouting notes.
This is our Rainmark station. Check what the weather actually did, and when.
And my Mailnest farm folder. Anything there that bears on the notices or the claims.

Back in Fieldmark. Give notice on every unit that needs it before its 72 hours are up, and file a claim on every harvested unit the policy pays, with the production and the amount. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

policy.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026, 10:00. Common Crop Insurance Policy (7 CFR 457.8) with the coarse grains crop provisions, Yield Protection, 75% coverage, 100% share. Topics: notice, causes, claim, prices. Only units on the acreage report are insured.

Basic Provisions §14: give notice of damage or loss by unit within 72 hours of your initial discovery of it, and not later than 15 days after the end of the insurance period. Damage found within 15 days of harvest: leave representative samples. One notice per unit and cause; a unit already noticed for a cause needs no second notice for it. A missed notice can leave the loss treated as uninsured.

Insured: unavoidable, naturally occurring events: drought, excess moisture, hail, wind, frost and freeze, insects and plant disease (unless control measures were not applied), wildlife, fire. Not insured (§12): negligence or mismanagement; failure to follow recognized good farming practices, such as a weed control pass that was skipped; acts of any person, such as chemical drift; failure or breakdown of irrigation equipment, unless an insured cause caused it.

Submit a claim within 60 days after the insurance period ends for all the unit's acreage, at harvest at the latest. Production to count is the harvested bushels on the scale tickets. Indemnity = (production guarantee - production to count) x projected price x share. A unit that produced its guarantee or more has no indemnity. A loss from an uninsured cause is not paid.
2026 projected prices on this policy: corn $4.60 a bushel, soybeans $10.80 a bushel.

fields.notes: Hail on 24 July shredded leaves at tasseling; scouted the next morning. Ear fill uneven.
Dryland field. 18 August: the first walk that pulled ears found them short, with tip-back from the drought; the first sign of yield loss on this unit, noticed to Fieldmark on 20 August.
Some stalks lodged after the 3 September wind; most picked up fine.
The pivot's center gearbox failed on 14 July from wear; parts back-ordered, running again 26 July. Crop went without water through the July heat.
Agronomist, 1 July: cupped, strapped leaves along the east edge, worst near the line, consistent with dicamba drift from the neighbor's soybean spraying on 28 June.

fields.status: Standing, stage R6 (full seed), harvest planned 2026-10-20
fields.notes: 7 October, 07:30: leaves frozen and wilted across the field after the overnight freeze; pods still green. Damage found on the first walk.

fields.status: Standing, stage R6 (full seed), harvest planned 2026-10-22
fields.notes: 8 October, 16:00: first walk after the freeze; leaves frozen, green pods, seed fill stopped.
Clean field, harvested before the freeze.
Hail on 20 September knocked pods off; scouted on the 21st. Harvested before the freeze.
Agronomist, 25 June: recommended a post-emergence herbicide pass for waterhemp. The pass was skipped while the sprayer was busy elsewhere; waterhemp overtopped the beans by August.
Kessler rental, lease signed 20 July. 8 October: leaves frozen after the freeze, green pods.
8 October, walked after the freeze: pods brown and dry, beans hard. No damage.

mail.subject: Sorry about the drift
mail.search: Gary Voss sorry drift spraying U-105
mail.body: Ines, my applicator sprayed dicamba on my beans on 28 June and it drifted onto your corn on the east line. My insurance company will be in touch. Gary

mail.subject: Freeze last night
mail.body: If the freeze hurt any standing beans, give notice in the portal within 72 hours of when you found it, unit by unit, and leave the samples. Mature beans usually come through a freeze fine.
